title: What the parties say on the courts
note: From Ynet's party-by-party survey on the judiciary, Sept 22, 2026. No published position found for Noam (checked October 2026).

rows.text: Declined to answer Ynet's questions, saying the party "does not participate in questionnaires."

The Supreme Court's president and deputy president chosen by a secret ballot of judges; split the attorney general's role into legal adviser and chief prosecutor; public hearings for nominees; a 61-vote override; limits on interim orders and on who may petition; laws struck down only by an expanded bench and a special majority. Zehut, Feiglin's party on the joint list, would abolish the selection committee and have voters elect justices directly.
Said it was still preparing a detailed judicial platform with legal experts and senior figures in the legal field.
Deri: "fundamentally reform the judicial system and return power to the people and their elected representatives." No detailed new platform.
Says the Supreme Court has accumulated excessive power and its authority needs to be reconsidered and more clearly defined.
The balance has shifted too far toward the courts; an additional judicial tier; remove the Israel Bar Association from the selection committee; narrow the reasonableness standard.

Repeal the judge-selection law and replace it through a Basic Law; opposes an override clause; clearer rules for judicial review through a Basic Law governing the judiciary, alongside a Basic Law on legislation.

Formally define the powers of the Knesset, government and Supreme Court; a Basic Law on legislation setting how Basic Laws are enacted and when the court may intervene; repeal the appointments law, which would politicize the court system; the Declaration of Independence as a Basic Law.
A written constitution put to a national referendum; amendments would need at least 80 of the Knesset's 120 members.
The urgent problem is delays, overloaded courts and a shortage of judges, not excessive judicial power; an intermediate court of appeals; a comprehensive definition of the separation of powers.

The judiciary holds too much power; regulate the Basic Laws more clearly while limiting the Supreme Court's ability to intervene in government decisions; more oversight of prosecutors; a stronger Knesset role in overseeing the executive.
First a Basic Law on legislation; an override only with more than 72 lawmakers; narrow, not abolish, the reasonableness standard; at least 61 votes to enact a Basic Law.
Supports reforms that strengthen democratic protections and safeguard the rights of all citizens; an appointment mechanism that preserves judicial independence.
Declined to give a current position; in 2023 it opposed the law abolishing the reasonableness standard and other measures to shift power from the courts.
